title: Risk, empirical risk, and the bias-variance split
brief: Build the pieces of empirical risk minimisation, then run a Monte Carlo experiment that verifies the bias-variance decomposition numerically.
hints: polynomial_features should return a matrix whose column j is x ** j, for j from 0 to degree inclusive, so that fit_polynomial can hand it straight to a least-squares solve.
fit_polynomial can call numpy.linalg.lstsq directly; this lesson is about the statistics, not the numerics of the solve, which lesson 2 covers.
bias_variance_decomposition should store one row of predictions per trial, shape (n_trials, len(x_query)), then take the mean and the variance down axis 0.
The noise term is just noise_std ** 2, broadcast to the shape of x_query; it does not depend on the trials at all.
train_test_split should shuffle a permutation of range(n) with a seeded numpy Generator, not the raw arrays, so the same permutation slices both x and y.
